item.title: LOT-173: Opt-in iCloud Keychain account sync and Face ID / code app lock

item.body:
### Summary

As a member with several Apple devices, I want to choose "Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud" so that my HFR accounts are available on my other devices without logging in again, and I want an optional Face ID / code lock on the app, so that someone holding my unlocked phone cannot open my forum accounts.

Operator decision 2026-10-28 (ADR 0013, Q12): accounts stay device-only by default (Keychain `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, LOT-065, Q-9); the sync is **opt-in**, and the app lock is optional. Security-sensitive: Opus-routed.

### Scope

- **Opt-in Keychain sync**: a switch in Settings (LOT-119 (#210)) "Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud", off by default, with a one-paragraph explanation (what travels: the session cookies and `hash_check` of each account; where: the user's iCloud Keychain, end-to-end encrypted by Apple; how to stop: switch off, which replaces the synchronizable copy with a tombstone and keeps the accounts of each device on that device). When on, `KeychainCredentialStore` (LOT-065) writes the credential envelope to a **second, synchronizable** Keychain item (`kSecAttrSynchronizable`, accessibility `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock`, since `ThisDeviceOnly` classes cannot sync); the device-only item stays the local master; switching off replaces the synchronizable item's envelope with a dated tombstone (the other devices keep their local copy and switch off when they read a tombstone not earlier than their own `enabledAt`; the absence of the item tells them nothing). A device with no local item that finds a full envelope newer than every tombstone it knows imports it (first launch on a new device); a tombstone imports nothing.
- **Rules of the copy** (ADR 0013 §6, as reviewed on PR #313): the device-only item is the master; bootstrap only from a full envelope (never from a tombstone or an absent item); divergence = `enabledAt` first (an item whose `enabledAt` is later than the device's own switches it off until the user switches on again explicitly, an earlier one is re-written by the device), then, with equal `enabledAt`, newest `updatedAt` wins the whole envelope, then `AccountBook.init(accounts:)` repair; an explicit switch-on over a full envelope adopts the item's `enabledAt` (never a new one) and merges the device's accounts into it by frozen account key, newest credentials per account winning (`updatedAt` per account), so two devices that each hold accounts stay on together; only a switch-on over a tombstone or an absent item sets a new `enabledAt`; switching off writes a dated **tombstone** envelope (`deletedAt`, no accounts), never deletes the item, and absence of the item proves nothing; every push is a read-compare-write where a tombstone whose `deletedAt` is not earlier than the device's `enabledAt` (the logical version set by the last explicit switch-on, carried unchanged by credential pushes; a tie switches off, there is no `lastPushed`) wins and switches the device off; a tombstone met at bootstrap keeps the switch off, is recorded as `honouredDeletedAt` and creates no device-only item; the accounts a bootstrap imports are marked imported, and the item is provisional until the first local credential change on the device (login or re-login) or the first read confirming the item still holds the envelope it bootstrapped from, whichever comes first: switched off while provisional, the device deletes only the imported accounts, never one entered on the device (the only case where switching off deletes credentials); a push never writes an `enabledAt` lower than the item's current one (fail closed); a tombstone older than the device's `enabledAt` is superseded by that explicit switch-on, and the device re-writes its full envelope over it under the switch-on read-compare-write, so no device stays silently stuck; only an explicit switch-on overwrites a tombstone, with an `enabledAt` strictly later than it; devices that honoured a tombstone (its writer included) keep reading while off and re-write it over a raced envelope whose `enabledAt` is older. Accepted residual risks (operator 2026-10-29): `enabledAt` and `deletedAt` are wall-clock dates, not a generation counter, so a device whose clock runs ahead can make an earlier switch-on outrank a later opt-out; and a fresh device that bootstrapped from a raced stale envelope, whose provisional window ended before the race repair arrived, switches off but keeps the imported credentials (on the user's own Apple-ID devices only). The maintainer confirms these rules in the spec.
- **App lock**: a switch "Verrouiller l'app (Face ID / code)", off by default, using `LocalAuthentication` (`LAContext`, `deviceOwnerAuthentication`: biometrics with passcode fallback); lock on launch and when returning after a grace delay (0 / 1 / 5 minutes); the app's content is hidden behind a cover view while locked and in the app switcher. No PIN of our own: the device passcode is the fallback.
- **Privacy manifest / entitlements** (LOT-160 (#250)): `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`; no new entitlement for Keychain sync (the data-protection Keychain item with `kSecAttrSynchronizable` needs iCloud Keychain on the device, not a capability).
- **Legacy**: no equivalent in the legacy app (accounts were `AfterFirstUnlock`, not synchronizable, audit E §2.1); the legacy Keychain item is read by LOT-067 and never made synchronizable.

- Module: App · Difficulty: medium · Priority: medium · post-MVP · security
- Implements: ADR 0013 (Q12, operator 2026-10-28)
- Legacy sources (read-only, `origin/master`): `Classes/MultisManager.m:43-86` (whole-blob Keychain item), `Carthage/Checkouts/SimpleKeychain/SimpleKeychain/A0SimpleKeychain.m:45` (`AfterFirstUnlock`)
- Spec: `docs/lots/LOT-173-*.md`

### Depends on

- LOT-065 (#90, done)
- LOT-081 (#99, done)
- LOT-119 (#210, done)
- LOT-160 (#250, done)

### Blocked by

none: every dependency is merged (unblocked 2026-10-29, steward ext/opus-helper1)

### Model

Opus → Fable (AGENTS.md §6: the reviewer is never the author model; security work is Opus-routed)

### Captures needed

- none (no HFR fact involved)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the switch off, no synchronizable Keychain item exists (test on a signed host, `HFR_KEYCHAIN_TESTS=1`); switching on creates exactly one, switching off replaces its envelope with a tombstone (`deletedAt`, no accounts) and never deletes the item; the device-only item is never changed by the switch (the imported accounts of a provisional bootstrap, dropped when the device is switched off before its first local credential change or confirming read, are the one exception); switching on over a full envelope adopts its `enabledAt` and writes the merged accounts (newest credentials per account key), and two devices that each hold accounts both stay on.
- [ ] A fresh install that finds a full synchronizable envelope imports the accounts and keeps the device-only item as master afterwards; one that finds a tombstone imports nothing, stays off, records `honouredDeletedAt` and creates no device-only item; one that finds a full envelope whose `enabledAt` is not later than a known tombstone imports nothing; one that bootstrapped from a racing stale envelope (no known tombstone yet) and is switched off by the repair while provisional deletes the imported accounts only, and keeps an account the user logged in on that device meanwhile.
- [ ] Interleaving test against an in-memory item: device A reads the envelope, device B switches off (tombstone at t=150), A pushes a credential change (t=160, stale `enabledAt`), B's next read re-writes the tombstone, A's next read-compare switches off; a tombstone with `deletedAt` equal to the device's `enabledAt` also switches it off; a device that reads an envelope with a later `enabledAt` than its own switches off instead of adopting it, and a push against such an item is refused; a device whose `enabledAt` is later than the tombstone it reads re-writes its full envelope over it; sync never comes back without an explicit switch-on.
- [ ] After a merge on switch-on, a tie on the envelope's `updatedAt` never leaves the other device's accounts unshared: the spec picks one of "the merge sets the envelope's `updatedAt` to now" or "*Divergence* merges per account when `enabledAt` is equal", and a test covers the case where the device holding the newest account is the one that reads the union.
- [ ] Per-account consent: a merge on switch-on never brings back an account deleted on another device (device D switched off while holding y, y deleted on B, D switched on again: y does not return); the spec defines the per-account rule (e.g. a per-account deletion marker with its date, honoured by the merge) and a test covers it.
- [ ] A race repair that reaches a bootstrapped device after its provisional window ended switches it off and deletes nothing (operator-accepted residual risk); a test covers both sides of the window.
- [ ] The lock covers every scene (including the app switcher snapshot) and every grace delay; a failed or cancelled authentication keeps the cover; the background MP check (LOT-140 (#230)) still runs while locked.
- [ ] Nothing logs a cookie or token; the explanation texts are in French and reviewed by the operator before merge.
- [ ] View logic lives in `@Observable @MainActor` models tested with Swift Testing in `App/SwiftHFRTests/`; each new test is shown to fail without the change.
- [ ] `xcodebuild build test` green on the iPhone 18 Pro and an iPad simulator (iOS 27.0), and the `App build + tests` CI job green; no new dependency.

### Before you start (agents and humans)

Read, in order: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/ORCHESTRATION.md, docs/agents/REVIEW-ROUNDS.md, docs/agents/LESSONS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, App/README.md, ADR 0012, ADR 0013, the spec of every dependency (docs/lots/). Claim with `/claim <session-id>` on this issue before writing code; PR body `Closes #<this issue>` + `Claim: <session-id>`; never guess HFR behaviour.
